knowledge_point.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle 3 u + 2 v + 2,u + 1,u - 2 v + 1\rangle.
$$

subject to $u^2+v^2\le 3$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrization over $D$, use $$
A(S)=\iint_D\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm dA
$$

Differentiate and form the fundamental vector product:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r_u&=\langle 3,1,1\rangle,\\\mathbf r_v&=\langle 2,0,-2\rangle,\\\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\3&1&1\\2&0&-2\end{vmatrix}\\&=\langle -2,8,-2\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=\sqrt{(-2)^2+(8)^2+(-2)^2}=6 \sqrt{2}.
$$

The constraint is a disk in the parameter plane with radius $\sqrt{3}$. Its area is $\pi(\sqrt{3})^2=3 \pi$.

The area scale factor is constant, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(S)&=\iint_D 6 \sqrt{2}\,\mathrm dA\\&=6 \sqrt{2}\cdot\operatorname{Area}(D)\\&=6 \sqrt{2}\cdot(3 \pi)=18 \sqrt{2} \pi.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle 2 u + v - 1,- u - v - 1,2 u + 3 v\rangle.
$$

subject to $u^2+v^2\le 2$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrization over $D$, use $$
A(S)=\iint_D\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm dA
$$

Differentiate and form the fundamental vector product:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r_u&=\langle 2,-1,2\rangle,\\\mathbf r_v&=\langle 1,-1,3\rangle,\\\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\2&-1&2\\1&-1&3\end{vmatrix}\\&=\langle -1,-4,-1\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=\sqrt{(-1)^2+(-4)^2+(-1)^2}=3 \sqrt{2}.
$$

The constraint is a disk in the parameter plane with radius $\sqrt{2}$. Its area is $\pi(\sqrt{2})^2=2 \pi$.

The area scale factor is constant, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(S)&=\iint_D 3 \sqrt{2}\,\mathrm dA\\&=3 \sqrt{2}\cdot\operatorname{Area}(D)\\&=3 \sqrt{2}\cdot(2 \pi)=6 \sqrt{2} \pi.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle - 3 u - 2 v,2 u + v + 1,- u + v\rangle.
$$

subject to $u^2+v^2\le 1$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrization over $D$, use $$
A(S)=\iint_D\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm dA
$$

Differentiate and form the fundamental vector product:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r_u&=\langle -3,2,-1\rangle,\\\mathbf r_v&=\langle -2,1,1\rangle,\\\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\-3&2&-1\\-2&1&1\end{vmatrix}\\&=\langle 3,5,1\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=\sqrt{(3)^2+(5)^2+(1)^2}=\sqrt{35}.
$$

The constraint is a disk in the parameter plane with radius $1$. Its area is $\pi(1)^2=\pi$.

The area scale factor is constant, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(S)&=\iint_D \sqrt{35}\,\mathrm dA\\&=\sqrt{35}\cdot\operatorname{Area}(D)\\&=\sqrt{35}\cdot(\pi)=\sqrt{35} \pi.
\end{aligned}
$$
